title: One Taiwanese injured in attack on Saudi Arabia airport: MOFA
summary: Taipei, Oct. 13 (CNA) Taiwan's government on Tuesday condemned a series of attacks targeting King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, last week that resulted in deaths and civilian casualties, adding that one Taiwanese national was injured in one of the attacks and hospitalized in Saudi Arabia.

title: Taiwan closely monitoring China pneumonic plague rumors: Premier
summary: Taipei, Oct. 13 (CNA) Taiwan's government will continue monitoring online rumors that a pneumonic plague outbreak has spread from Russia into China and may strengthen existing quarantine measures, Premier Cho Jung-tai (卓榮泰) said Tuesday.

title: MOFA security checks uncover China-developed software
summary: Taipei, Oct. 13 (CNA) The Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MOFA) said Tuesday it is cooperating with an ongoing investigation into a Taiwanese software company suspected of repackaging China-developed software and selling it to the ministry for use on computers at Taiwan's overseas offices.

title: 12 mayoral candidates sign sustainability pledges ahead of elections
summary: Taipei, Oct. 12 (CNA) Twelve candidates in Taiwan's upcoming local government elections have signed pledges to promote sustainable and resilient policies if elected, civic groups said Monday.

title: PLA drills not close to Taiwan: Defense Minister Koo
summary: Taipei, Oct. 12 (CNA) Defense Minister Wellington Koo (顧立雄) said Monday that Taiwan is closely monitoring China's military exercises in the region and has assessed that the latest round will be held off the coast of China rather than near Taiwan.

title: Lai's National Day speech steady, avoided provoking Beijing: Scholar
summary: Taipei, Oct. 11 (CNA) President Lai Ching-te's (賴清德) National Day address maintained a steady stance on cross-strait issues while reaffirming Taiwan's commitment to peace, a political science scholar said Sunday, adding that the speech gave Beijing no pretext for military coercion or provocation.
